headline: Gold and silver ETFs rally up to 6% as MCX prices rebound from recent losses
hook: Precious metals bounce back from oversold levels

modes.bear: Persistent US inflation and looming Federal Reserve rate hikes could trigger further downside risks for bullion.
modes.bull: Bargain buying and short covering indicate strong underlying support for precious metals following oversold conditions.
modes.simple: Gold and silver ETFs jumped up to 6% as prices bounced back from a recent drop. Experts suggest using SIPs instead of chasing sudden spikes.

summary: Gold and silver ETFs surged up to 6% on Thursday, led by gains in HSBC Gold ETF and DSP Silver ETF due to bargain buying and short-covering after a two-day slide. MCX gold futures rose to Rs 1,23,673 per 10 grams and silver climbed to Rs 1,48,336 per kg, despite strong US inflation data strengthening expectations of a Federal Reserve rate hike. Analysts suggest retail investors use SIPs for long-term allocation while staying cautious ahead of the upcoming FOMC meeting.
why_it_matters: Gold and silver ETFs recover ground after recent sharp correction.
winners_losers: Precious metal holders gain / late chasers hurt
